The first release of `s4`, an `mc`-style command line client for S3 storage and the companion client for the S4 server. It is one small binary with no libraries to install: HTTP goes through `curl` and the AWS SigV4 signature through `python3`, both of which a Linux machine already has. Every command is covered by the integration suites, which pass against both S4 and MinIO.

## ✨ New

- **Buckets and objects**: `ls`, `mb`, `rb`, `put`, `get`, `rm`, `stat`, `cat`, `head`, `find`, `tree`, `cp` and `mv`, plus `pipe` to stream stdin straight into an object.
- **`sync` and `mirror`**: the `mc mirror` workflow with `--remove`, `--exclude`, `--newer-than`/`--older-than`, `--dry-run` and `--watch`. Objects whose size and ETag already match are skipped, and inside one account the data is copied server-side instead of travelling through your machine.
- **Large files**: from 16 MiB up everything goes through multipart upload, and the part size grows with the file so an upload always fits into the 10000-part limit. `pipe` streams stdin instead of holding the object in memory.
- **Bucket settings**: `cors`, `encrypt`, `event`, `legalhold`, `retention` and `sql` (S3 Select), with `ping` and `ready` to check an endpoint.
- **Aliases**: `alias set|ls|rm` keep endpoints and keys in `~/.s4/config.toml`.
- **Made for scripts**: `--json` output for every command, plus `--debug`, `--limit-upload`, `--limit-download`, `--custom-header`, `--resolve` and `--insecure`.
- **Packages**: `.deb` for Debian and Ubuntu (amd64, arm64) and tarballs for x86_64 and aarch64.

## 🔒 Security

- The secret key and every request header, `Authorization` included, are handed to `curl` and `python3` on stdin, so they never appear in the process list. The one exception is `alias set`, whose arguments are visible while it runs, as with any command line tool.
- `~/.s4/config.toml` is written atomically with mode `0600`, and a config found with wider permissions is tightened when it is read.
- Temporary files live in a private per-process directory with mode `0700` and are removed when the command exits.
- Nothing destructive happens quietly: `rb` refuses a bucket that still has objects unless `--force` is given, governance retention is overridden only with `--bypass`, and `sync` removes objects at the destination only with `--remove`.
- A download writes to a hidden file next to the destination and replaces the target only after it succeeded, so an interrupted `get` never leaves a truncated file behind.

## ⬆️ Before the first command

- `curl` 7.55 or newer and `python3` have to be in `PATH`.
- This build speaks path-style addressing only, so create aliases with `--path-style`:

  `s4 alias set local http://127.0.0.1:9000 ACCESS_KEY SECRET_KEY --path-style`

- Known server gaps, neither of them a bug in `s4`: S4 does not implement bucket notifications yet (`event add`/`event rm` answer with `409`), and MinIO answers `501` for `cors`, needs a configured KMS for `encrypt set` and an existing target ARN for `event add`.
